{{One source|date=April 2026}}
In [[algebraic K-theory]], '''Quillen's resolution theorem''' states that if <math>\mathcal{A}\subset\mathcal{C}</math> is an exact [[subcategory]] where <math>\mathcal{A}</math> is an extension-closed subcategory of <math>\mathcal{C}</math>, which is also closed under taking kernels of admissible surjections, and has a finite resolution by objects in <math>\mathcal{A}</math>; then the inclusion <math>\mathcal{A} \rightarrow \mathcal{C}</math> induces a [[homotopy]] equivalence of their K-theory spectra <math>K_0(\mathcal{A})\simeq~K_0(\mathcal{C})</math>.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ogawa |first=Yasuaki |last2=Shah |first2=Amit |date=2024-11-15 |title=A resolution theorem for extriangulated categories with applications to the index |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0021869324003223 |journal=Journal of Algebra |volume=658 |pages=450–485 |doi=10.1016/j.jalgebra.2024.05.041 |issn=0021-8693}}</ref>
